historic_survey.note: Recorded under the name Young Men's Institute.

historical_record.description: The Filipino Youths Organization and Filipino Schools were here in 1935.

Built in 1914 for the Young Men's Institute to the design of William Shea: a Beaux Arts steel-and-concrete building of four to five storeys over a two-level basement, rising 75 to 87 feet and 97 at the parapet, with three-storey terra cotta Ionic columns and a decorative sheet-metal cornice under terra cotta ornament, a ballroom on the first floor and a gymnasium and swimming pool below. Its frieze reads 'The Young Men's Institute Building and Donahue Library'.
The Young Men's Institute and the Young Ladies' Institute occupied the building from 1914 until 1995, when the Archdiocese sold it; it was later known as the International Center.

Built in 1923 by the firm of Shea and Shea as an adjunct to the institute building next door, holding a new gymnasium, handball courts and meeting rooms for local chapters: a concrete and brick block of three to four storeys, 53 to 77 feet high, plainer than its neighbour, its cornice carried on heavy flat banding that answers the fretwork on the base of 50 Oak Street. To fund it the organisation sold the deed of 50 Oak Street to the Archdiocese of San Francisco. It was cleared for the Conservatory of Music's new wing.
